title: Independent neuron route counts gave no clear response prediction gain in 13987 selected worm pairs
abstract: We tested whether the number of independent internal-neuron routes improves evoked calcium response detection prediction in selected C. elegans cell pairs. We linked two adult wiring maps to the Randi wild-type atlas by cell name. The sample had 13,987 pairs and 721 detected responses. Whole stimulated cells were held out of training. Controls included endpoint degree, two-step routes, shortest paths, observation count and cell identity. Adding the mean log route count changed log loss from 0.183120 to 0.182948. The reduction was 0.000172, with a conditional 95 percent shared-cell bootstrap interval from -0.000549 to 0.000834. The result gives no clear added value under the tested model. The two anatomy maps and the pooled response atlas came from different animals. Aggregate detection, fixed-prediction uncertainty, correlated controls and incomplete neuron coverage limit inference. Code, cut tables, linked features, predictions, source hashes and checks support reproduction.

display.caption: Added route-count prediction gains. Bars show conditional 95 percent shared-cell bootstrap intervals. Positive values mean lower held-out log loss.

citations.reason: We reuse the published primary chemical cut table and independently check 100 cuts per adult.
We extend its same-pair benchmark to internal-neuron routes of any length; no code is reused.
